basics.summary: Senior Software Engineer with 13+ years of experience in system integration, legacy modernization, and distributed systems. My focus is bringing well-structured product architecture, reducing technical debt, and making complex systems more understandable and easier to test. 70% of my workflow is AI-assisted — from code analysis and refactoring to tests and prototypes.

wins.title: Legacy Modernization at Revizto
wins.context: A large BIM/CAD desktop platform with 10+ years of accumulated legacy code. Core business logic tightly coupled to UI, undocumented domain knowledge, fragile under change.
wins.problem: Adding features took weeks due to ripple effects across tightly coupled modules. No automated tests meant regression bugs on every release. Domain knowledge was siloed in senior developers' heads.
wins.solution: Reverse-engineered legacy code into documented domain modules. Introduced service layer separating business logic from UI. Built automated test harness around critical workflows. Applied AI-assisted analysis to accelerate knowledge recovery.
wins.result: Significantly fewer regression bugs. Domain knowledge formalized in code and docs. Test coverage reached 60%+ on critical paths.

wins.title: Smartcat Drive — New Platform Core with Hierarchical Structure
wins.context: Localization platform stored thousands of files as flat lists. Every file operation was individual and manual.
wins.problem: Flat file lists didn't scale. Customers managed thousands of files with no organizational structure. Bulk operations (move, copy, delete, tag) were impossible. No API existed for file and folder operations — every interaction went through the UI.
wins.solution: Built Smartcat Drive — a new core platform kernel replacing flat lists with hierarchical folder/file structure. Designed an abstract DOM-like model where any entity (file, folder, external system object) is a node in a tree. Built a dedicated Drive API for programmatic file/folder interaction. Implemented bulk operations across the tree structure.
wins.result: The platform got a proper hierarchical file system kernel. Files and folders became abstract nodes — any external system object could be represented in the tree. The Drive API enabled programmatic interaction with the file structure. Bulk operations automated key file workflows.

wins.title: Media Workflow Automation
wins.context: Localization platform expanding into multimedia. Customers needed video/audio localization — transcription, subtitle generation, dubbing. Each media format required different processing pipeline.
wins.problem: No existing media processing infrastructure. Video files are large (multi-GB), processing is slow and resource-intensive. Multiple third-party tools (ffmpeg, transcription APIs) need orchestration.
wins.solution: Built Docker-based media processing microservices with async job queues. Created format-agnostic pipeline: ingest → transcribe → translate → generate subtitles/dubbing → deliver. Used AST-based format conversion for subtitle formats.
wins.result: Introduced media processing capability from scratch — the platform had no video/audio/subtitle support before. Supported virtually any media format via ffmpeg-based pipeline. Enabled new revenue stream — media localization became a paid add-on.

wins.title: Electronic Signature & Government Document Automation
wins.context: Russian engineering design institute required by law to submit project documentation to government expertise review with electronic signatures. Documents are multi-GB engineering projects with strict format requirements.
wins.problem: Manual document preparation took 3-5 days per submission. Russian cryptographic standards (GOST) different from Western PKI. Errors in signature placement caused document rejection by government systems.
wins.solution: Built automated document assembly pipeline: CAD data → PDF → structured document package → GOST electronic signature → government portal submission. Integrated Russian cryptographic libraries with .NET-based workflow engine.
wins.result: Processing time reduced from 3-5 days to under 2 hours. Document rejection rate dropped by 80%. System processed thousands of documents.

wins.title: Integration Hub — From Months to 2 Weeks per Integration
wins.context: Localization platform needed to integrate with 15+ external systems (Zendesk, Contentful, Google Docs, AWS, GitHub, Figma, Okta, Jira). Each integration required months of custom development with tightly coupled adapters.
wins.problem: Integration development was slow (months per system), brittle under API changes, and each adapter was a one-off with no shared infrastructure. Adding a new integration was a major engineering investment.
wins.solution: Built 2 generations of integration hub: v1 — quick Kubernetes-based prototype proving the hub concept; v2 — hierarchical provider architecture with shared base classes, standardized authentication, and pluggable data transformers. Each new integration becomes a provider implementing well-defined interfaces.
wins.result: New integration time dropped from months to 2 weeks. 15+ integrations unified under single architecture with web UI for managing and monitoring all external system connections. Old brittle adapters fully deprecated. Integration autotests ensure reliability across all external system interactions.

wins.title: CadFerma — Multi-CAD Validation Platform
wins.context: Engineering design institute used multiple CAD tools (Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD) for railway, highway, building, and structure design. Each tool had its own proprietary format and validation logic. Engineers manually checked designs across tools — slow, error-prone, and inconsistent.
wins.problem: No unified way to validate engineering data across different CAD systems. Each CAD tool operated in isolation. Validation rules were applied manually per tool. Switching between tools to cross-check a single design took hours.
wins.solution: Built CadFerma - a web service orchestrating multiple CAD applications (Revit, Civil 3D, AutoCAD) under a single plugin-based interface. It loaded models from each tool, ran cross-tool validation checks, and produced unified compliance reports, replacing hours of manual cross-referencing.
wins.result: Engineers could validate designs across multiple CAD tools through a single web interface. Cross-tool validation time dropped from hours to minutes. Automated checks replaced manual cross-referencing. Plugin architecture allowed adding new CAD tools and validation rules without changing core service logic.
